summary:
Aeolis: A Mars Science Expedition is a story-driven 3D game set in Gale Crater. Players become field geologists investigating an orbiter’s clue that water may have altered Martian rocks. They choose a science objective and compatible telescope design, learning how mission goals shape engineering trade-offs. Planning is interactive.

Players traverse procedural terrain using astronaut movement, jumping, sprinting, and a fuel-limited jetpack. Changing daylight and dust storms shape the expedition. At three sites, they collect basalt, clay-bearing rock, and dune samples, then return to the lander to uplink results and complete the story.

The project connects launch, spacecraft and relay operations, surface exploration, and science analysis. Its journal introduces simplified concept development and verification stages. The game was built in Godot with GDScript.

Aeolis is inspired by NASA mission-design, GMAT, Mission Viz, and telescope-design resources. It does not use live NASA datasets or APIs, nor connect to GMAT or Mission Viz. Orbital displays and telemetry are simulated; the story is fictional. Procedural terrain and a built-in astronaut model keep the prototype playable without optional art assets.
details:
Aeolis: A Mars Science Expedition is a 3D game set in Gale Crater. Players are field geologists testing whether water altered Martian rocks. They plan observations by matching a science goal with a wavelength, instrument, and telescope design, then explore three sites, collect samples, and uplink results to Earth.

The game features procedural terrain, astronaut movement, a jetpack, changing daylight, dust storms, and a mission HUD. Its journal connects launch, spacecraft and relay operations, surface work, and science analysis. Each sample advances a story about Mars’s changing environment.

Aeolis makes mission planning and planetary science approachable through play. Instrument trade-offs, field evidence, communication, and science return become choices and actions. The design prioritizes clear controls, a manageable scope, and a link between player decisions and mission outcomes.

Built in Godot with GDScript, the prototype uses generated terrain and a simple astronaut model; it includes no external images or 3D models. NASA mission-design, GMAT, Mission Viz, and telescope concepts informed its design. It uses no live NASA datasets or APIs; orbital displays and telemetry are simulated.
